clue.text: Late work by Charles Williams lets Mr Caine in on this, a day later

indicators.note: the clue says Mr Caine is let in, so his name goes inside the word for lets

parts.note: to let someone do something is to allow them
Hall Caine was a popular Victorian novelist

explanation.surface: A literary note dating a Charles Williams novel and a festival that follows it by one day.
explanation.walkthrough: Williams's 1945 novel is All Hallows' Eve; 'on this, a day later' says the answer is the feast that comes the day after that Eve, 1 November. The writer to know is Hall Caine, not the actor Michael Caine.
explanation.definitionFit: The feast of All Saints on 1 November follows the Eve that names the Williams novel.

clue.text: Bow introducing a recent cinema organist

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next four words introduce them, so their heads are taken

explanation.surface: A bow given to welcome a cinema organist who has just started.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, arco is the instruction to play a string instrument with the bow rather than plucking.

clue.text: Tall fee may be obtained from tract

indicators.note: the answer may be got from these words only by rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A writer's tall fee earned from a single tract.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short pamphlet on a religious or political subject, the kind of printed sheet handed out.

clue.text: Lent partly for Eliot's poetry day

definitions.text: Lent partly for Eliot's poetry day

parts.words: Lent partly for Eliot's poetry day
parts.note: a day that is the opening part of Lent, and also the title of a T. S. Eliot poem of 1930

explanation.walkthrough: The day that begins Lent shares its name with Eliot's 1930 religious poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The first day of Lent is also the title of Eliot's poem sequence.

clue.text: Murder mystery twins deprived of property

definitions.meaning: Neville and Helena are the twins in Dickens's unfinished murder mystery The Mystery of Edwin Drood
having no land or estate to one's name

explanation.walkthrough: The Drood twins' surname is also an ordinary adjective for someone owning no land.
explanation.definitionFit: The Drood twins' surname also describes someone owning no estate; both senses share one spelling.

clue.text: Swift described "old Charon's" as leaky, in a quibbling elegy

definitions.text: Swift described "old Charon's" as leaky, in a quibbling elegy

parts.words: Swift described "old Charon's" as leaky, in a quibbling elegy
parts.note: Jonathan Swift's punning elegy mentions the leaky boat of Charon, ferryman of the dead

explanation.surface: Jonathan Swift mocking the ferryman of the dead in a punning poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Charon rows the dead across the Styx; the boat named here is a light rowing boat once used to ferry passengers on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A light rowing boat for passengers fits Charon's job of ferrying the dead.

clue.text: Inevitable for time, Huxley thought

parts.note: Aldous Huxley's novel Time Must Have a ... names what time must have

explanation.surface: Aldous Huxley musing on what time cannot avoid.
explanation.walkthrough: Huxley's 1944 novel takes its title from Shakespeare: 'Time Must Have a Stop', so the word that completes the title is what time must have.
explanation.definitionFit: Huxley's title says time must have an end or halt, so a halt is inevitable for it.

clue.text: Novel, yet saintly knight

definitions.meaning: Simon, the hero of Leslie Charteris's novels, is known as The Saint
a member of the medieval military order based at the Temple in Jerusalem

explanation.surface: A fictional knight who is nonetheless a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: Simon of the Charteris novels is nicknamed The Saint; the crusading order shares his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Charteris's Saint is also the title of a knight of the crusading Temple order.

clue.text: Attorney supplying fruit drink to builder

parts.note: perry is an alcoholic drink made from fermented pears
a mason builds in stone

explanation.surface: A lawyer bringing drinks to a man on a building site.
explanation.walkthrough: PERRY, pear cider, is a British country drink. Erle Stanley Gardner's courtroom hero is the attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: Erle Stanley Gardner's fictional defence lawyer is the best-known attorney in crime fiction.

clue.text: Bennett's fighter with sword

parts.note: Cassius Clay was the boxer later known as Muhammad Ali
a hanger is a short sword once hung from the belt

explanation.surface: A Bennett character who fights with a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bennett's' stands for a novel by Arnold Bennett: his 1910 book named after its hero Edwin.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold Bennett's novel of the Potteries is titled with its hero's surname, so it is a work of his.

clue.text: Back-rhyme, say, for potentate

indicators.note: back tells us to write the word for rhyme from right to left

parts.note: rime is an old spelling of rhyme, and 'say' marks it as a variant form

explanation.surface: A verse device written backwards, offered to a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns RIME round. 'Back-rhyme' looks like a term of prosody, but the hyphen only joins the indicator to its word.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or prince, a powerful sovereign.

clue.text: Rich cake followed by disturbed siesta is ancient history

indicators.note: the cake comes first and the remaining letters follow it

parts.note: an Eccles cake is a rich pastry filled with currants, from Lancashire

indicators.note: a disturbed nap has its letters thrown about

explanation.surface: Eating a rich cake before a broken afternoon nap is old news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges SIESTA to IASTES. An Eccles cake is a small British currant pastry. The Bible book recounts ancient wisdom, so 'ancient history' defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: The book of the Preacher is an ancient scriptural text, part of Old Testament wisdom literature.

clue.text: Sort of bloomer made by Penelope Fitzgerald

definitions.text: Sort of bloomer made by Penelope Fitzgerald

parts.words: Sort of bloomer made by Penelope Fitzgerald
parts.note: Fitzgerald's last novel is The ... Flower, a kind of bloom named by its colour

explanation.surface: A novelist making a gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a flower here, not a mistake; Fitzgerald's 1995 novel about Novalis is The Blue Flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour in Fitzgerald's title describes a kind of flower, so it is a sort of bloomer.

clue.text: How Wordsworth and Coleridge wrote ballads

definitions.text: How Wordsworth and Coleridge wrote ballads

parts.words: How Wordsworth and Coleridge wrote ballads
parts.note: their joint collection of 1798 was titled Lyrical Ballads, so the adverb describes the manner of writing

explanation.surface: A question about the two Romantic poets' method.
explanation.definitionFit: Their joint collection was called Lyrical Ballads, so they wrote the ballads in a songlike manner.

clue.text: Underfed tailor begins with top billing

definitions.meaning: a starved, thin creature is underfed
Robin, the tailor in A Midsummer Night's Dream, has a surname starting with the word for a top-billed performer

explanation.surface: A hungry tailor who opens a show as its headliner.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shakespeare tailor's name starts STAR, which is what 'top billing' gives.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-starved creature is underfed, and Shakespeare named his thin tailor in the mechanicals' play for that.

clue.text: Big girl bested by Zeus

definitions.meaning: a female giant of Greek myth, a very large woman
Zeus overthrew the elder giant gods, of whom she was one

explanation.surface: A large young woman beaten by the king of the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: A female of the giant gods is huge, and Zeus defeated that race in the war of the gods.

clue.text: Halo not applicable for Elizabeth!

indicators.note: the clue reads the answer as Elizabeth's title less the abbreviation, so that abbreviation is removed from it

parts.note: Gloriana was the poetic name for Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a saintly halo does not suit Elizabeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Take NA off Elizabeth I's name, GLORIANA, as used by Spenser in The Faerie Queene.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloria is a halo or aureole of light round a holy figure's head in painting.

clue.text: His Without Prejudice possibly written with pride

definitions.text: His Without Prejudice possibly written with pride

parts.words: His Without Prejudice possibly written with pride
parts.note: Israel's collection of essays Without Prejudice (1896) recalls Austen's pairing of pride with prejudice

explanation.surface: A writer proud of a book called Without Prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without Prejudice' looks like the legal phrase but is the 1896 essay collection by Israel Zangwill's author; Austen paired prejudice with pride.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel of that surname wrote the 1896 essays Without Prejudice, which echo Austen's famous title.

clue.text: More has happened, including this new version of work

indicators.note: the phrase includes the answer within it, across its words

explanation.surface: Someone noting further events when a work is revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' points at the run across 'moRE HAS Happened'.
explanation.definitionFit: To recycle old material in new form is to rework it, and the noun names that warmed-over revision.

clue.text: Dawn's gaunt rider

parts.note: Henry Rider, author of the first novel Dawn (1884), has a surname that means gaunt

explanation.surface: A thin horseman setting out at daybreak.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawn is the 1884 first novel of H. Rider Haggard, author of She; his surname also means gaunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Rider is the middle name of the author of Dawn, and his surname also describes a careworn, gaunt face.

clue.text: Singer, a maiden loved by Zeus, is merchant's friend

parts.note: a bass sings the lowest male part
an is the form of the indefinite article before a vowel
Io was a maiden loved by Zeus and turned into a heifer

explanation.surface: A singer and a mythical beloved of Zeus count as friends of a trader.
explanation.walkthrough: The merchant is Antonio in The Merchant of Venice, who borrows from Shylock for his friend.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Venice play, Antonio borrows money so his close friend can woo Portia.

clue.text: "In guid time comes an antidote / Against sic poison'd —" (Burns)

definitions.text: "In guid time comes an antidote / Against sic poison'd —" (Burns)

parts.words: "In guid time comes an antidote / Against sic poison'd —" (Burns)
parts.note: the missing word completes the Burns couplet and names a quack remedy

explanation.surface: A Burns couplet about a timely cure with its last word blanked.
explanation.walkthrough: The gap rhymes with nothing given; it is filled by a word for a quack medicine, set against an antidote.
explanation.definitionFit: Burns sets a quack cure against a true antidote, and the word for that dubious remedy completes the line.

clue.text: No drop of her blood was human, was said by Rossetti of this wife of Adam

definitions.text: No drop of her blood was human, was said by Rossetti of this wife of Adam

parts.words: No drop of her blood was human, was said by Rossetti of this wife of Adam
parts.note: Rossetti's sonnet Body's Beauty speaks of Adam's first wife, the woman of Jewish legend before Eve

explanation.surface: Rossetti describing Adam's inhuman first wife.
explanation.walkthrough: In Jewish legend Adam had a first wife before Eve; Rossetti's poem Eden Bower calls her not of human blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend gives Adam a first wife before Eve, and Rossetti wrote of her as a serpent-woman.

clue.text: Art that should make a good impression

definitions.text: Art that should make a good impression

parts.words: Art that should make a good impression
parts.note: an art of cutting designs into metal plates to print impressions from them

explanation.surface: Advice to look one's best at a first meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: An impression is a printed copy from a cut plate, not the effect one has on people.
explanation.definitionFit: The craft cuts a design into a plate from which printed impressions are taken.

clue.text: A later addition at East end

definitions.text: A later addition at East end

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is something added after the letter
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A note about something added afterwards at the east end of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the semicircular recess at a church's east end was often a later addition.
explanation.definitionFit: A church's recess is usually at its east end, often built on later.

clue.text: Paul Morel (before he was a lover)

definitions.text: Paul Morel (before he was a lover)

parts.words: Paul Morel (before he was a lover)
parts.note: Paul is the hero of Lawrence's Sons and Lovers

explanation.surface: A character in Lawrence's novel before his romances.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawrence's title Sons and Lovers puts son before lover, so Paul is 'a son' first.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul is his mother's child in Sons and Lovers before he takes lovers.

clue.text: She succumbed to a kiss from the queen

definitions.text: She succumbed to a kiss from the queen

parts.words: She succumbed to a kiss from the queen
parts.note: in Antony and Cleopatra the attendant dies after Cleopatra's farewell kiss

explanation.surface: A woman fainting at a royal kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: In Antony and Cleopatra, Cleopatra kisses her maid farewell and the maid falls dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra's attendant dies after the queen's farewell kiss in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Illustrations for Little Women?

parts.note: small paintings, the size that would suit little people

explanation.surface: Pictures for Louisa May Alcott's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Alcott's novel is a red herring: the pictures are small, the scale for little women.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny detailed paintings would be the right size for little people.

clue.text: Novelist and soldier of the French

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A writer who is also a French soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: André Gide was the French novelist of The Immoralist.
explanation.definitionFit: André Gide was a French novelist and Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Mary Shelley presented him, Jessica Anderson later produced his head

definitions.meaning: Mary Shelley's 1826 novel about the sole survivor of a plague

definitions.text: Jessica Anderson later produced his head
definitions.meaning: Jessica Anderson's 1970 crime novel is titled with this phrase plus Head

explanation.surface: Two women writers each producing a man, one only his head.
explanation.walkthrough: Shelley's novel and Anderson's The Last Man's Head share the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelley's novel title is the same phrase that, with Head, titles Anderson's crime novel.
